page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the right margin (scripture references and section numbers). The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: ec[?] eorum jugo colla nostra subducamus, eo sci-cet prætextu[?], quod meri homines sint, & crea-tæ, sicut & nos, {1}κτίας ἀνθρωπίνη[?], filii Adæ, 1 Pet.2.13. mortale genus, iisdem omnino affectibus, per-turbationibus, infirmitatibus, casibus, quibus & nos obnoxii. Quin potiùs memores, Deum Opt. Max. eos nobis cum delegatâ potestate velut suos in terris Vicarios præfecisse, ipsosque propterea tanto honore dignatum esse, ut eis & nomen suum quasi visibilibus & mortalibus quibusdam Diis, communicaverit {2}[Ego dixi, Dii estis] par est ut eos summa cum reverentia colamus, honoremus, obsequamur. Etsi non ipsorum gratia; qui, ut homines sunt, pari nobiscum conditione sunt, nec de meliore luto effecti; at Divinæ tamen ordinationis intuitu, qui eos quâ principes sunt, sublimiore loco esse voluit quàm reliquos homines, & suæ potestatis aliquatenus participavit. Διὰ τὴν ἐξουσίαν[?], ut alibi Petrus; & ex confequenti διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν[?], ut hic loquitur Apostolus Paulus.Psal. 82.6,

XXIII. CONCLUSIO QUINTA. Leges humanæ rite constitutæ, etiam in particulari, etsi non directè & per se, ex consequenti tamen & virtute generalis præcepti Divini, obligant (subdi-torum conscientias. Dico primo, Leges rite consti-tutas. I. Id est, & ratione Causæ efficientis: ab eo, qui legitimâ potestate præditus est, latas: & ratione Materiæ; nil illicitum, inhonestum, turpe, aut officio hominis Christiani quomodolibet contrarium, imperantes. Jam enim diximus eas Leges, quæ utrovis nomine peccant, non obligare. Dico secundo, In particulari: id est, quantum ad determinationem particularem in rebus mediis aliquæ. Ut quale & quantum tributum sit solvendum; 2. quæ merces liceat aut non liceat è regione expor-tare; In Academia qui habitus quibus gradibus competant;

page.notes: Mark {1} and {2} stand in the text and the margin notes repeat them as printed ("1 Pet.2.13.", "Psal. 82.6,"). Scripture reference marks are printed as superscript numerals. Doubtful readings: "ec" at the start of the page is a fragment with the first letter hidden in the gutter; "prætextu" (possibly misprinted); both Greek phrases in the text ("κτίας ἀνθρωπίνη" and the two "διὰ" phrases) are uncertain and marked [?]. The "Paulus." line under the column is set small and italic and is read as the end of the sentence. "competant;" is read as the last line of the sentence, not as a catchword. The left-edge text and the lower-left fragments belong to the neighbouring page and are excluded. Section numbers "I." and "2." in the right margin are listed as notes.
